title: Coherent log ideals and their unsaturated and saturated chart gluings
statement:
Let $(Y,N)$ be a locally Noetherian fs log scheme and $\mathcal H\subset N$ a nonempty coherent log ideal [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Its algebraized ideal $K=\alpha(\mathcal H)\mathcal O_Y$ is a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent], and on every strict etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ with fine saturated monoid chart $P\to A$ and $\mathcal H$ generated by a finite nonempty set $E\subset P$, its pullback is $(\alpha(e):e\in E)\subset A$. Use additive notation for $P$, and put $Q_e=\langle P,h-e\ (h\in E)\rangle\subset P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ and $Q_e^{\mathrm{sat}}=\{q\in P^{\mathrm{gp}}:nq\in Q_e\text{ for some }n>0\}$. Both $Q_e$ and $Q_e^{\mathrm{sat}}$ are finitely generated integral monoids with group completion $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$. For a monoid $T$, $\mathbf Z[T]$ denotes the ring of finite sums of symbols $z^t$ with $z^tz^{t'}=z^{t+t'}$. The fine log schemes with charts
$$\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q_e])$$
glue on their common localizations, and descend along strict etale covers, to a fine log scheme $Y_0\to Y$ universal for making $\mathcal H$ locally principal among fine log schemes. Replacing every $Q_e$ by $Q_e^{\mathrm{sat}}$ gives compatible charts that glue and descend to an fs log scheme $Y_s\to Y$ with the corresponding universal property among fs log schemes. There is a canonical morphism $s:Y_s\to Y_0$; it is finite on underlying schemes (preimages of affine opens are spectra of finite algebras). These constructions commute with strict etale restriction. Tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Here a fine log scheme has etale-local charts by finitely generated integral monoids, without a saturation requirement; a log morphism is strict when its source log structure is the one associated to the inverse image of the target log structure and its structure map.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.17--3.1.21, printed pp. 100--101; 3.2.9, printed p. 104 (finiteness of saturation); 3.3.5--3.3.9, printed pp. 107--108 (chart construction, descent and universal properties); 3.4.2, printed p. 110 (algebraized monoidal ideal).

proof.text: Algebraize the ideal. On a strict etale chart with generators $E$, every section of $\mathcal H$ is locally $e+p+u$ with $e\in E$, $p\in P$ and $u\in\mathcal O^\times$, so its image is $\alpha(e)\alpha(p)u$. Conversely each $e$ lies in the ideal. Hence its image generates exactly $J_E=(\alpha(e):e\in E)$. This ideal and its inclusions into the structure sheaf agree on chart overlaps, since they are both the ideal generated by the same image sheaf $\alpha(\mathcal H)$. Etale covers are fpqc covers by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale]; effective descent and full faithfulness for quasi-coherent modules in [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] descend these ideals and inclusions to a quasi-coherent ideal $K\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$. Faithful flatness reflects the injectivity of these inclusions, so its image is precisely the stipulated image ideal. Finite type is local for this cover: over an affine base choose a finite affine fpqc refinement, use its faithfully flat product algebra, and apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-descent-finite-module] to the module of the descended ideal. The generators on this refinement are the finitely many images of the corresponding $E$. Thus $K$ is of finite type in [pqf-def-coherent], with the asserted chart formula.

source.place: VIII 3.3.7 and 3.4.2, printed pp. 107 and 110; module descent: Stacks Tag 023T; finite-module descent: Tag 03C4.

proof.text: Fix one chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$. A finite generating set for $P$, together with the finitely many $h-e$, generates $Q_e$. Since $P\subseteq Q_e\subseteq P^{\mathrm{gp}}$, the monoid is integral and its group completion is exactly $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$: the two inclusions generate the same group. Apply [lem-trf-fine-monoid-finite-saturation] to $Q_e$. It gives all the asserted properties of $Q_e^{\mathrm{sat}}$, including finite generation, the same group completion, and a finite set $F_e$ such that $Q_e^{\mathrm{sat}}=\bigcup_{f\in F_e}(f+Q_e)$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17--3.1.21, printed p. 101; 3.2.9, finiteness sentence, printed p. 104.

proof.text: For $T=Q_e$ or $Q_e^{\mathrm{sat}}$, form $B_T=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[T]$ and give $\operatorname{Spec}B_T$ the log structure associated to the monoid map $t\mapsto1\otimes z^t$. Explicitly it is the associated-log pushout of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] at each stalk, so this is a chart by $T$. The inclusion $P\to T$ and the map $A\to B_T$ define the log morphism to $U$. By the definition of a fine (respectively fs) chart these are fine (respectively fs) log schemes. Their pulled-back log ideals are generated by $e$: for every $h\in E$, $h=e+(h-e)$ and $h-e\in T$, while $e$ is one of the original generators. This concerns a principal monoid ideal even when $\alpha(e)$ is zero or a zero-divisor.

source.place: VIII 3.3.5--3.3.8, printed p. 107 (strict chart base change and principalization).

proof.text:
For $e,f\in E$, inside $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ one has
$$Q_e+\mathbf N(e-f)=Q_f+\mathbf N(f-e).$$
Indeed $h-f=(h-e)+(e-f)$ and $h-e=(h-f)+(f-e)$, while the adjoined elements are mutually inverse. Thus localizing $\mathbf Z[Q_e]$ at $z^{f-e}$ and $\mathbf Z[Q_f]$ at $z^{e-f}$ gives the same monoid algebra. Tensoring with $A$ preserves this equality of the presentations (both are obtained by adjoining a variable inverse to the same monomial). These identify the corresponding principal open subschemes and their chart log structures. The same construction works with saturated monoids by localization compatibility in [lem-trf-fine-monoid-finite-saturation]. On a triple overlap all three identifications are the identity in the common localization inside $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$, so the cocycle condition holds. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes] to obtain schemes $U_0$ and $U_s$, and glue their log sheaves by these log isomorphisms. The associated-log pushouts agree on overlaps, so the glued sheaves satisfy the log-structure condition and have the displayed fine or fs charts. Their maps to $U$ and their principal pulled-back ideals agree on overlaps as well.

source.place: VIII 3.1.19 and 3.3.5--3.3.9, printed pp. 101 and 107--108; scheme gluing: Stacks Tag 01JB.

proof.text: Prove the universal property of $U_0$ explicitly. Let $g:(T,M_T)\to U$ be any fine log morphism making the pulled-back ideal locally principal. Etale locally it is $m+M_T$. At a stalk write $g(e)=m+a_e$ for $e\in E$; since $m$ belongs to the ideal generated by these images, $m=g(e)+b$ for some $e$. Cancellation in the integral monoid gives $a_e+b=0$, so $a_e$ is a unit and this $g(e)$ generates the ideal. After etale shrinking, all $g(h)-g(e)$ are sections of $M_T$. The group homomorphism $P^{\mathrm{gp}}\to M_T^{\mathrm{gp}}$ induced by $g$ therefore restricts to $Q_e\to M_T$. Composing with the structure map gives $\mathbf Z[Q_e]\to\mathcal O_T$, compatible with the given $A$-map; the tensor presentation defines a scheme map to $\operatorname{Spec}B_{Q_e}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. Its monoid map defines the log lift via the associated-log pushout. Any such lift must send $h-e$ to $g(h)-g(e)$ by cancellation, so it is unique on this locus. If both $e$ and $f$ generate, $g(f)-g(e)$ is a unit and the two lifts agree in precisely the overlap of Step 4. Descent of fine log morphisms in [lem-trf-polarized-fine-log-etale-descent] glues the lifts uniquely. Conversely every morphism to $U_0$ pulls back its principal log ideal. This proves existence and uniqueness for exactly the fine test objects claimed.

For an fs test object in Step 5, every stalk of $M_T$ is saturated in its group completion. To see the chart implication, for an fs chart $R$ take its face of elements mapping to units. [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening] identifies the characteristic monoid with the saturated quotient of its face localization. Thus if $nx$ lies in $M_T$, its class lies in this saturated characteristic monoid, and a lift differs from $x$ by a unit; hence $x\in M_T$. For $q\in Q_e^{\mathrm{sat}}$, a positive multiple $nq$ belongs to $Q_e$, so its group image lies in $M_T$ by this saturation property. This extends $Q_e\to M_T$ uniquely to $Q_e^{\mathrm{sat}}\to M_T$ (the ambient group map is already fixed). Stalkwise membership gives sheaf membership. The monoid-algebra and tensor presentation of Step 5 now gives the unique lift to the saturated chart. On overlaps it agrees by Step 4, and descent of log morphisms gives the lift to $U_s$. Conversely its ideal is principal by Step 3. This proves the fs universal property without imposing conditions on the images $\alpha(e)$.

The two local constructions commute with strict etale restriction. Indeed the restricted log structure is obtained by pulling back the same chart, the same monoids $Q_e$ or $Q_e^{\mathrm{sat}}$ occur, and each algebra is obtained by the same tensor presentation with the restricted structure ring. Hence the chart and overlap maps pull back to exactly those of Step 4. The universal properties in Steps 5--6 identify any two constructions using different charts or generating sets on the same base: each has a unique morphism to the other, and both composites are the identity by uniqueness. These comparisons commute with further strict restriction and satisfy the cocycle condition, since both composites on a triple overlap are the unique map with the same universal property. No identification of an etale overlap with an affine localization is needed here.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8, middle paragraph (compatibility with strict morphisms), printed pp. 107--108.

proof.text: Supply the polarization needed for scheme descent. On either local glued scheme let $\mathcal J$ be the principal pulled-back log ideal. Its generators form a torsor under $M^\times=\mathcal O^\times$: if $a+M=b+M$, cancellation gives mutually inverse differences $a-b$ and $b-a$, hence a unique unit relating the two generators. Glue free line modules with frames $v_e$ by $v_f=\alpha(f-e)v_e$ on the overlaps. The reciprocal and triple identities of Step 4 show directly that this is an invertible module $L$. Every $h\in E$ defines a section $s_h$ by $s_h=\alpha(h-e)v_e$ on the $e$-chart. The formula $h-e=(h-f)+(f-e)$ proves compatibility. Its nonvanishing locus is exactly the $h$-chart: on the $e$-chart it is $D(z^{h-e})$, the overlap with the $h$-chart. These finitely many affine nonvanishing loci cover the glued scheme, so $L$ is ample over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. After any affine base change the same finite affine loci and sections give the same criterion, so $L$ is relatively ample over $U$. Its construction from the generator torsor of $\mathcal J$ makes it independent of the chart: the comparisons of Step 7 identify $\mathcal J$ and its generators, hence identify $L$ canonically, with the cocycle condition. The calculation applies to both $U_0$ and $U_s$.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8, final sentence, printed pp. 107--108, expanded scheme descent; ampleness criterion: Stacks Properties Tag 01PS.

proof.text: Choose a strict etale affine chart cover of $Y$ on which $\mathcal H$ has the stipulated finite generating sets; this is part of coherence and the fs chart condition in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. On double overlaps use Step 7, and equip these comparisons with the compatible relatively ample line bundles of Step 8. Apply [lem-trf-polarized-fine-log-etale-descent] separately to obtain the fine log scheme $Y_0$ and the fs log scheme $Y_s$ over $Y$ with exactly these local charts. The scheme-effectivity hypothesis is satisfied by the line bundles, rather than inferred from arbitrary etale scheme descent. For any fine test object over $Y$ with principal pulled-back ideal, pull back the chart cover to that test object and apply Step 5. The local lifts agree by uniqueness and descend by the morphism clause of the same descent theorem. Conversely a lift pulls back the principal ideal on $Y_0$. The same argument with Step 6 proves the universal property of $Y_s$ among fs test objects. Uniqueness also identifies these global constructions with their strict etale restrictions.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.9, printed pp. 107--108; effective polarized descent as specified in the cited generic descent node.

proof.text: Since $Y_s$ is fine and its pulled-back ideal is principal, the universal property of $Y_0$ gives a canonical morphism $s:Y_s\to Y_0$. On the $e$-charts it is induced by $\mathbf Z[Q_e]\to\mathbf Z[Q_e^{\mathrm{sat}}]$. The preimage of the $e$-chart of $Y_0$ is the $e$-chart of $Y_s$: in either construction this open is precisely the locus where $e$ generates the pulled-back log ideal, as the unit criterion and overlap calculation show. By [lem-trf-fine-monoid-finite-saturation], the former ring extension is a finite module generated by the monomials $z^f$ for $f\in F_e$. After tensoring with $A$, the finitely many $1\otimes z^f$ still span, by the defining balanced tensor relations. Thus over each strict etale chart of $Y$ the morphism $s$ is finite on the affine cover of $U_0$ by its $e$-charts. These affine charts over all $U$ form an etale cover of $Y_0$, hence an fpqc cover by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-finite] to deduce global finiteness. It means exactly that every affine open has affine inverse image with a finite algebra. The canonical map and all chart descriptions commute with strict etale restriction by Step 7 and uniqueness.
